description: REAL big-data I/O + CPU task: build an EGFR structure-activity (QSAR) model from the full ~6GB BindingDB dump. Stresses DISK/IO (parsing a 6GB TSV) then CPU (RDKit Morgan fingerprints + RandomForest QSAR). Multi-turn: load -> filter -> clean -> fingerprint -> model -> report. First task designed to characterize the I/O axis (needs the disk_read_mbps/ram_used_gb sampling added to trace_run.py).
prompt:
You are given the real BindingDB dump at data/biomni_data/data_lake/BindingDB_All_202409.tsv -- a ~6 GB tab-separated file of measured protein-ligand binding affinities (194 columns; each row = a ligand with its SMILES, a target protein with UniProt ID, and measured Ki/IC50/Kd/EC50 in nM). Goal: build a structure-activity (QSAR) model for the drug target EGFR. Keep code simple and defensive; report concrete numbers and TIMINGS at each step.

1. Load the file efficiently. It has 194 columns and duplicate column names (one UniProt block per target chain), so select columns BY INDEX to avoid ambiguity: use pandas.read_csv('data/biomni_data/data_lake/BindingDB_All_202409.tsv', sep='\t', header=0, usecols=[1, 6, 8, 9, 42], dtype=str, on_bad_lines='skip', engine='c'). Those indices are: 1=Ligand SMILES, 6=Target Name, 8='Ki (nM)', 9='IC50 (nM)', 42='UniProt (SwissProt) Primary ID of Target Chain'. Rename them to smiles, target_name, ki_nM, ic50_nM, uniprot. TIME this load with time.time() and report both the number of rows loaded and the load time in seconds (the file is large -- the load is a real I/O + parse cost we care about).
2. Filter to EGFR: keep rows where uniprot == 'P00533' OR target_name contains 'Epidermal growth factor receptor' (case-insensitive). Report how many EGFR binding records remain.
3. Build the activity label: prefer IC50 (nM), else Ki (nM). Parse the numeric value (strip any leading '>', '<', '~', ' ' and coerce to float; drop rows that don't parse or are <= 0). Convert to pIC50 = 9 - log10(value_in_nM). Report the number of usable (smiles, pIC50) pairs and the pIC50 distribution (min / median / max).
4. For each UNIQUE ligand SMILES, compute a Morgan fingerprint (radius 2, 2048 bits) with RDKit (from rdkit import Chem; from rdkit.Chem import AllChem). Drop SMILES that RDKit cannot parse. If a SMILES appears multiple times, average its pIC50. Report how many fingerprint/activity pairs you built.
5. Train a QSAR model on the fingerprint matrix (X = np.array of the fingerprints, y = pIC50). Use sklearn RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, n_jobs=4, random_state=42) and get out-of-fold predictions with sklearn.model_selection.cross_val_predict(model, X, y, cv=3) (do NOT also fit a separate full model -- one 3-fold pass is enough). From the out-of-fold predictions report the R2 (sklearn.metrics.r2_score) and the RMSE. Also list the 10 most potent EGFR ligands (highest pIC50) with their SMILES.

Finally report: total BindingDB rows loaded AND the load time in seconds, number of EGFR records, number of usable ligand-activity pairs, the pIC50 min/median/max, number of fingerprints, the cross-validated QSAR R2 and RMSE, and the top 10 potent ligands.
notes: FIRST I/O-characterization task (2026-08-10). Two distinct heavy phases to profile separately with the new sampling: (A) LOAD phase = read/parse a 6GB 194-col TSV -> disk_read_mbps spike + CPU parse + ram_used_gb climb; the prompt makes the agent TIME and report the load. (B) COMPUTE phases = RDKit Morgan fingerprints on ~13k EGFR ligands + RandomForest QSAR. FIX (2026-08-10): first single-agent run FAILED -- RF n_estimators=300/n_jobs=1/cv=5 on 13114x2048 = ~40min single-threaded -> hit MAX_WALL_SECONDS=1200. Bounded to n_estimators=100/n_jobs=4/cv=3 via cross_val_predict (~2min). Everything BEFORE the RF worked (load warm 36s, 24816 EGFR rows, 22862 pIC50 pairs, 13114 fingerprints, pIC50 median 6.93) -- only the RF was over-sized. Multi-turn. WATCH: usecols=[1,6,8,9,42] by INDEX because BindingDB has duplicate column names (UniProt block repeats per target chain); dtype=str because affinity cols carry '>'/'<' prefixes. PAGE CACHE: first cold run shows real disk_read_mbps; warm re-runs read from RAM (~0 disk) -- run cold for I/O numbers, or note warm behaviour. MEMORY: usecols keeps only 5 cols (~2-3GB) but the 6GB read buffer + fingerprint matrix add up -> at CONCURRENCY this is an OOM item (worse than DepMap). DEP: needs rdkit (core to biomni cheminformatics; verify present). Validate single-agent with MAX_WALL_SECONDS=1200. Data at data/biomni_data/data_lake/BindingDB_All_202409.tsv (sync to MN5 before scale).
